Sound familiar?

Love isn’t the problem. The loop is.

  • The apology happens, and the same fight is back a week later.
  • One of you reaches out, and the other goes quiet.
  • Bringing anything up turns into defending instead of listening.
  • You keep wondering whether to stay and work on it, or leave.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

Why the apologies aren’t working

What real repair looks like, and why “sorry” on its own keeps the cycle going.

How to spot the anxious-avoidant cycle

See your attachment pattern and your partner’s, so the push and pull stops feeling personal.

What to do in the first 10 minutes after a fight

Simple ways to regulate emotions before the conversation spirals.

How to handle a defensive partner

How to raise something hard without chasing, shutting down or keeping score.

What couples who repair well do differently

The habits partners who successfully repair their relationship build, and how to start one this week.

Script 1 · “The apology”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Here’s why so many apologies don’t actually fix anything.”

Body

“An apology ends the fight. It doesn’t repair it. When one partner is anxious and the other is avoidant, ‘sorry’ often just pauses the cycle until next week. Repair is a different skill, and it can be learned.”

CTA

“I’m teaching it live in a 60-minute masterclass. It’s $17, the replay is included. Tap Sign up to grab your seat.”

Shot: talking to camera, same setup as your “Why the Apologies aren’t working” reel.

Script 2 · “The quiet partner”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Why do some partners go quiet right after a fight?”

Body

“It’s usually not that they don’t care. For an avoidant partner, conflict can feel like being cornered, so they pull back. Then the anxious partner reaches harder, and the loop gets tighter. Once you can see the cycle, you can step out of it.”

CTA

“In the Secure Partner Masterclass I’ll show you how. Live, 60 minutes, $17. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera, on-screen text “the cycle” highlighted in red.

Script 3 · “What repairers do”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Couples who repair well all do this one thing differently.”

Body

“They don’t wait until they feel calm to come back to the conversation. They have a way back in. A few words, a simple plan, and they use it every time. That’s what makes the next fight shorter.”

CTA

“I’ll walk you through it in my live masterclass. Seats are $17. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to slide with the 3 steps listed.

The apology happens. The silence follows. The same fight comes back next week.

That’s not a communication problem. It’s the anxious-avoidant cycle.

One partner reaches. The other retreats. Both end up feeling alone.

Most couples stop at “sorry”. The ones who make it learn to repair.

Repair is a skill. It has steps. It can be learned.Attachment, conflict repair, regulating emotions.
